quiz.question: What idea is Cobb hired to plant in Robert Fischer’s mind?
quiz.explanation: The mission is to persuade Fischer to dissolve his father’s conglomerate.

quiz.question: What does Saito promise Cobb in exchange for completing the job?
options: A new identity as a chemist
A way home to his children
quiz.explanation: Saito offers to clear Cobb’s criminal status so he can return to his children.

quiz.question: Who designs the architecture of the team’s three dream levels?
quiz.explanation: Ariadne designs the dream environments; Cobb avoids the job because Mal’s projection could sabotage them.

quiz.question: Whose dream provides the rainy city in the first level?
quiz.explanation: Yusuf dreams the rainy city that forms the first level.

quiz.question: Why does Fischer’s subconscious attack the team?
options: He has been trained to defend against dream intrusion
Saito has already told him the plan
quiz.explanation: Fischer has subconscious defensive projections because he has been trained to anticipate intrusion.

quiz.question: Under Yusuf’s powerful sedative, where does dying in a dream send someone?
quiz.explanation: The sedative prevents the usual wake-up and sends the dreamer into Limbo.

quiz.question: Where is Arthur’s second-level dream set?
quiz.explanation: The second level is a hotel dreamed by Arthur.

quiz.question: Who impersonates Fischer’s godfather Peter Browning?
quiz.explanation: Eames uses Browning’s identity to introduce the idea of an alternate will.

quiz.question: What early event forces Arthur and Eames to improvise their synchronized kicks?
quiz.explanation: Yusuf drives off the bridge too soon, forcing the other dream levels to adjust their kicks.
evidence_markers: Yusuf performs his kick too soon

quiz.question: What does Cobb do before seeing the final result of the spinning top?
quiz.explanation: Cobb goes to his children before observing the result; the quiz does not claim the ending proves dream or reality.

facts.title: A hallway that really turned
facts.text: The hotel corridor was a physical set that rotated through 360 degrees, making the changing gravity part of the actors’ performance.

facts.title: Explosions without explosives
facts.text: For the Paris café sequence, the crew used high-pressure nitrogen because local authorities would not allow real explosives.

facts.title: A train built for the street
facts.text: The street-chase train was built on a tractor-trailer chassis, using fiberglass molds taken from real train parts.

facts.title: A fortress in miniature
facts.text: The effects team built a miniature mountain fortress and blew it up for the film, combining practical work with digital effects.

facts.title: A familiar guitarist in the score
facts.text: Former Smiths guitarist Johnny Marr played on Hans Zimmer’s score. Zimmer also worked elements of Édith Piaf’s song into the music.
